## Pull request overview

Completes multiple DX roadmap deliverables by adding new developer tooling (CLI + VS Code extension), expanding Studio DX components, and restructuring documentation so curated/hand-written content lives under `content/docs/guides/` while `content/docs/references/` remains auto-generated.

**Changes:**
- Added a new VS Code extension package (`packages/vscode-objectstack`) with snippets, hover help, and basic config diagnostics.
- Added new CLI commands (`lint`, `diff`, `codemod v2-to-v3`) and wired them into the main CLI.
- Migrated/curated documentation from `references/` into `guides/`, added Contracts docs, and reinforced the auto-generation boundary in build scripts and Cursor rules.

`jsonValidation.url` points to `./schemas/objectstack.schema.json`, but this package currently has no `schemas/` directory, so VS Code won't be able to load the schema at runtime. Add the missing schema file (and ensure it's included in the VSIX) or update the path/URL to a file that actually ships with the extension.

`FIELD_TYPE_DOCS` includes values that don't match the actual `FieldType` enum in `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (e.g. `integer`, `uuid`, `geo_point`, `encrypted`) and misses others that do exist (e.g. `toggle`, `radio`, `checkboxes`, `tree`, `summary`). This will show incorrect hover info. Consider sourcing this list from `@objectstack/spec/data` (or generating it) to keep it in sync.

The code generators emit `defineStack({ objects: { ... } })` (and similarly for views/flows/agents/apps), but the config schema in this PR models these as arrays (e.g. `objects: [{ name, ... }]`). Exported code will not match the expected config shape. Consider exporting `objects: [ ... ]` etc (or updating the schema/CLI to accept the object-map form).

The `defineStack()` parsing path assumes `objects/views/flows/...` are object maps and uses `Object.entries(evaluated[key])`. In this PR's config schema those are arrays, so a typical `objects: [{...}]` config won't import correctly. Consider supporting the array form (and updating the placeholder example accordingly).

Comment says this “safely evaluate[s] the object literal using Function constructor”, but the implementation uses regex transforms + `JSON.parse` and never calls `Function`. Either update the comment or implement the intended evaluation approach (with appropriate sandboxing/constraints).
```suggestion
    // Parse the object literal string using the parseObjectLiteral helper
```

`name` is documented as snake_case, but the pattern allows a leading underscore (`^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`). In `packages/spec/src/shared/identifiers.zod.ts`, snake_case identifiers must start with a letter (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`). If this schema is meant to be generated from `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, it should match the source regex to avoid IDE accepting invalid names.

The CLI examples here reference commands/options that don't exist in this repo (`objectstack lint --deprecations` and `objectstack migrate`). The closest existing behavior appears to be `objectstack doctor --scan-deprecations` and `objectstack codemod v2-to-v3`. Update the docs to reflect the actual CLI surface so readers don't hit dead ends.
```suggestion
npx @objectstack/cli doctor --scan-deprecations

# Apply codemods to migrate from v2 to v3
npx @objectstack/cli codemod v2-to-v3
```

`validateConfigFile` only validates if the file is already open in an editor (`workspace.textDocuments`). When the watcher fires for a closed `objectstack.config.ts`, diagnostics will silently not update. Consider reading the file from disk (e.g., `workspace.fs.readFile`) or opening it via `workspace.openTextDocument(uri)` before validating.

`FIELD_TYPES` includes values that are not valid `FieldType` options in `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (e.g. `rollup`, `encrypted`, `geolocation`, `external_id`). This can lead to generating invalid metadata. Consider deriving this list from the spec `FieldType` enum (or renaming to the supported values like `summary`/`location`, etc.).
```suggestion
  { value: 'summary', label: 'Rollup', description: 'Aggregate child records', icon: Calculator, category: 'System' },
  // Advanced
  { value: 'json', label: 'JSON', description: 'Structured JSON data', icon: Braces, category: 'Advanced' },
  { value: 'text', label: 'Encrypted', description: 'Encrypted sensitive data', icon: Lock, category: 'Advanced' },
  { value: 'location', label: 'Geolocation', description: 'Latitude/longitude coordinates', icon: MapPin, category: 'Advanced' },
  { value: 'rating', label: 'Rating', description: 'Star rating field', icon: Star, category: 'Advanced' },
  { value: 'text', label: 'External ID', description: 'Unique external identifier', icon: Fingerprint, category: 'Advanced' },
```

The `fields.*.type` enum here doesn't match the spec `FieldType` enum (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`). For example this schema includes `integer`, `slug`, `uuid`, `ip_address`, `geo_point`, `encrypted`, but the spec includes values like `toggle`, `radio`, `checkboxes`, `tree`, `avatar`, `summary`, `location`, etc. This will make IDE validation disagree with runtime validation; the schema should be regenerated or updated to stay in sync with `FieldType.options`.
